financial_anchor.caveat: FY2026 pre-tax operating income governs the hurdle; net income and prior-year EBIT-scale proxies are excluded.

ai_claim.claim: Nike A.I.R. is a named generative-design exploration with athletes; demand forecasting and allocation remain an unverified hypothesis in this packet.
ai_claim.stage: E1 creative capability for A.I.R.; E0 for demand-forecast deployment
ai_claim.scope: Creative concept generation under athlete, brand and design rights; no production demand-planning scope is sourced.
ai_claim.limitation: A.I.R. does not support demand-forecast deployment, quality-adjusted sell-through improvement or retained cash.

strongest_counterevidence.claim: Adidas and fast-moving direct brands and marketplaces with their own demand data can replicate tools or force gains through to customers.
strongest_counterevidence.limitation: Competitive capability does not by itself prove equal outcomes.

rights_limit: Member and commerce data are subject to consent and privacy rules; wholesale sell-through data can be incomplete. Creative and athlete rights are contract-specific.
materiality_summary: Five percent of FY2026 operating income is $189.85m on an annual pre-tax basis; public evidence does not establish an AI-attributed amount.

arithmetic.inputs: FY2026 operating income $3.797bn; 5%; illustrative eligible SG&A/operations pool $3bn, efficiency 10%, realization 50%, retention 50%, recurring cost $60m
arithmetic.result: Illustrative $15m is below the $189.85m annual pre-tax hurdle; avoided markdown requires matched seasons and is not evidenced by A.I.R.

g2_provisional: Open: E1/E2 evidence supports measurement, but E3 quality-adjusted causality and E4 cash retention are not established.
